message:
Reflect using-declarator targets and enforce [expr.reflect]/7.2 (#353)

* Reflect the introduced function when an id-expression names a using-declarator

`^^derived::operator()` was rejected with "cannot take the reflection of
a using-declarator" whenever the call operator reached `derived` through
`using base::operator();`. [expr.reflect]/5.1 makes such lookups
ill-formed only for the `^^ reflection-name` form, whose terminal name
is an identifier; an operator-function-id, conversion-function-id or
template-id can only be the `^^ id-expression` form, which
[expr.reflect]/7 resolves like any other id-expression and so names the
function that the using-declaration introduced.

Apply the using-declarator rejection only to identifiers without
template arguments, and otherwise reflect the target of the shadow
declaration, in each of the three places that see one: direct lookup
of the operand, a dependent operand that instantiates to a
`DeclRefExpr`, and a dependent operand that instantiates to a
`UsingDecl`. `-fentity-proxy-reflection` is unchanged and still reflects
the using-declarator itself.

Fixes #342

Signed-off-by: Philip Craig <689193+philipcraig@users.noreply.github.com>

* Test the unqualified id-expression form with operator new

`&operator()` is ill-formed for a non-static member function, so
[expr.reflect]/7.2 rejects `^^operator()`. `operator new` is a static
member function, so it covers the same code path without the test
depending on a check that is not implemented.

Signed-off-by: Philip Craig <689193+philipcraig@users.noreply.github.com>

* Reject reflections whose '&id-expression' is ill-formed

[expr.reflect]/7.2 requires '&id-expression' to be well-formed when the
id-expression of a reflect-expression names an overload set. Enforce it
for operator-function-ids, conversion-function-ids and template-ids in
two cases:

- A non-static member function named without a nested-name-specifier,
  such as '^^operator()' in a class body: '&' cannot form a pointer to
  member from an unqualified name.
- A function template named without template arguments, such as
  '^^S::operator()' for a call operator template: with no target, '&'
  cannot select a specialization. A reflection-name that names a
  function template still represents the template ([expr.reflect]/5.5.2).

The check runs wherever the previous commit reflects the target of a
using-declarator, and also where no using-declarator is involved. It
replaces an assertion failure for '^^operator()' in a class template
that inherits a call operator template through 'using T::operator();'.

The libc++ tests that reflected an operator function template by name
now reach it with template_of on a specialization.

Signed-off-by: Philip Craig <689193+philipcraig@users.noreply.github.com>

* Apply the unqualified member function check to identifiers

A reflection-name that finds neither a template nor a type is
interpreted as an id-expression ([expr.reflect]/5.9), so '^^fn' for a
non-static member function 'fn' named without a nested-name-specifier
is ill-formed for the same reason as '^^operator()': '&fn' does not form
a pointer to member.

This rejects the 'this->[:^^fn:]()' idiom inside a member function; the
splice tests now spell it '^^S::fn'.

Signed-off-by: Philip Craig <689193+philipcraig@users.noreply.github.com>

* Complete reflection id-expression overload resolution

Signed-off-by: acassagnes <acassagnes@bloomberg.net>

* Fix regressions

Signed-off-by: acassagnes <acassagnes@bloomberg.net>

---------

Signed-off-by: Philip Craig <689193+philipcraig@users.noreply.github.com>
Signed-off-by: acassagnes <acassagnes@bloomberg.net>
